subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical configured-model health check now, and how should it relate to fallback-chain testing and staged model migration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this adds a new live CLI probe mode that overlaps open fallback-chain and model-migration diagnostics; automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Add Status Probe All
options.body: Implement `--probe --all` in `models status` as the configured-model health check while documenting how it differs from fallback-chain testing.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Fallback Diagnostics
options.body: Use the fallback-chain or model-migration work as the canonical surface and keep this issue linked as one use case.

options.title: Defer Live Probe Expansion
options.body: Keep the current provider/auth probe behavior until maintainers decide the cost, rate-limit, and JSON-output contract for broad live probing.

recommendation.title: Add Status Probe All
recommendation.body: Implement `--probe --all` in `models status` as the configured-model health check while documenting how it differs from fallback-chain testing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the existing model status probe and adjacent provider/auth behavior.
